title: Model arch perf notes - Llama / Mistral / Qwen (long-context + MoE routing)
content:
Status: working notes / perf investigation (informal).

Summary:
- Scope: focused profiling for Llama-family (7B/13B), Mistral (7B/8xK), and Qwen (14B/32k) in long-context regimes (4k, 16k, 32k) and interactions with MoE routing (routing overhead, imbalance, memory movement).
- Goal: identify primary bottlenecks in GPU latency/throughput, quantify cost of long-context KV handling, and assess MoE routing overhead at different batch/seq sizes.
- Quick takeaways: attention KV-materialization + softmax/attention kernels dominate for dense models at seq > 8k; MoE adds non-trivial dispatch/scatter-gather cost and CPU-GPU roundtrips when routing sits on CPU. Qwen-specific tokenizer/rotary differences increase memory churn.

Testbed / config:
- HW: NVIDIA A100 80GB (DGX-style), 8 GPU multi-node tests for MoE serving; single-node A100 for dense model microbenchmarks.
- SW: serving-runtime branch: perf/multi-kernel-2026 (PR 412), torch 2.1 + cutlass-backed kernels, custom attention kernels (fused attention + rotary) enabled for Llama/Mistral.
- Models: llama-13b (dense), mistral-7b (dense, grouped FFN layout), qwen-14b-32k (long-token-aware positional handling), moe-70b-like (8 experts simulated; top-2 gating).
- Workloads: 1) short conv bursts (<=512) 2) medium long (4k) 3) very long (16k, 32k) with batch sizes {1,2,4,8} and request concurrency to simulate streaming vs one-shot.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory allocs, memcpy counts, kernel times (nvprof/Nsight ranges), host-GPU memcpy times.

Benchmark highlights (representative):
- Llama-13B dense, batch=1:
  - seq=512: token-latency ~45ms (p50), tokens/sec ~22
  - seq=4096: token-latency ~210ms (p50), tokens/sec ~9
  - seq=16384: token-latency ~1.2s (p50), tokens/sec ~2.5
  - dominant: KV-read/write and attention softmax kernel (softmax scales quadratically in seq for naive implementations); our fused-attn reduces constant but still O(L^2) memory pressure.

- Mistral-7B, batch=2, seq=8k:
  - observed slightly better tokens/sec vs Llama at same dims (~10-15%), likely from denser MLP packing and smaller attention scratch memory.

- Qwen-14B-32k, batch=1:
  - seq=32k cold-start token-latency p50 ~3.8s, p95 ~5.2s
  - high memory churn from extended positional handling and tokenizer pre-processing; KV-cache memory allocation/fragmentation noticeable in our allocator (see logs).

MoE routing results (simulated 8 experts, top-2 gating):
- Baseline (routing on CPU): routing decision + host-side gather/scatter -> additional 30-120ms per token depending on batch/seq: host-GPU roundtrips and serialized memcpy were main culprit.
- GPU-routing (gating + dispatch kernels on GPU): reduces routing overhead to 6-20ms per token and removes host-GPU sync points.
- Dispatch cost: scatter/gather + all-to-all for multi-GPU expert placement dominates at scale. For 8 experts across 8 GPUs, all-to-all network cost becomes non-negligible when batch*seq large.
- Imbalance: top-2 gating produced uneven expert load (hot experts ~2x average). This creates queuing and reduces throughput by 18-35% unless we augment with capacity factor or overflow routing.

Profiling artifacts / hot kernels (observations from nvprof / Nsight):
- Attention_fused_forward: heavy GPU time for seq>4k (softmax and matmul).
- KV_copy_kernel: many small memcpy calls when we materialize KV cache per-request; high PCIe/IB bandwidth usage for host-side caching fallbacks.
- MoE_dispatch: expensive when implemented as separate scatter/gather steps; large index shuffles allocate temporary buffers and trigger allocator overhead (cudaMalloc/cudaFree hotspots).
- Rotary/pos-embedding transform: Qwen 32k path has extra kernels to remap rotary embeddings across chunks -> adds ~5-8% wall time for long contexts.

Root causes (pattern-level):
1) Memory movement > compute for long-context: we spend majority of time moving KV and intermediate tensors between kernels and between host/GPU when cache misses or when routing on host.
2) Kernel fragmentation: repeated small kernels (per-layer softmax, remap, transpose) cause kernel launch overheads and multiple kernel-to-kernel memops. Fusing reduces overhead significantly.
3) MoE routing on CPU: serialized routing decisions and host-side scatter/gather create synchronization points and extra memcpy.
4) Expert imbalance + all-to-all network: causes stragglers and head-of-line blocking across multi-GPU serving pools.

Mitigations tried and results:
- Fused attention + rotary kernel (single kernel per layer): ~20-35% improvement in p50 for seq 4k-16k on Llama/Mistral.
- GPU-side gating and dispatch (PR 412): routing overhead reduced by ~3-6x compared to CPU gating for large seq. Implemented as two kernels: gating (softmax/topk) + dispatch (scatter) with pre-allocated contiguous buffers.
- Pre-allocated per-request KV slabs: reduce cudaMalloc/cudaFree churn -> lowers p99 jitter for long sessions.
- Capacity-factor + overflow routing: mitigate expert hot spots; balancing reduces p95 tail by ~15%, throughput improved ~10% for skewed inputs.
- Batched KV read/write: amortize KV access across tokens in a microbatch; improves tokens/sec for high-concurrency workloads (batch >=4).

Remaining open issues / TODOs:
- Investigate further Qwen tokenizer/rotary pre-processing to push more of that work into GPU kernels and avoid host staging. Logs show significant CPU time in token->ids conversion at long seqs; potential to offload chunking to CUDA.
- All-to-all optimization: explore NCCL topology-aware all-to-all + compression (float16 dispatch buffers) to reduce network overhead for MoE multi-node setups.
- Improve allocator behavior for large-seq KV slabs: current allocator fragments for mixed-size requests; evaluate buddy allocator or per-request pool.
- Routing cache (route decisions): prototype caching gating outputs for prefix tokens (where gating is stable) to avoid recomputing routing every token — needs correctness check for top-2 dynamic gates.
- Measure power/thermal at sustained long-context runs (observed thermal throttling in one DGX with seq 32k, causing ~5% perf drop over 30min).

Quick action plan (next 4 weeks):
1) Merge GPU-routing PR (412) to perf branch; run end-to-end regression suite across 7B/13B/14B long-context models. (Owner: Diego)
2) Add fused-attn+rotary fallback for Qwen long-context path to reduce remap kernels (Owner: Priya).
3) Prototype routing cache TTL and evaluate on synthetic traces with stationary prefix gating (Owner: Ava).
4) Experiment with NCCL all-to-all tuning and float16 dispatch to quantify network savings (Owner: Ethan).
5) Add allocator telemetry to production perf runs to capture cudaMalloc/cudaFree rates per-request (Owner: infra-team).

Notes / random observations (scratch):
- For streaming workloads (token-by-token), amortize CPU overhead by batching gating decisions every N tokens when safe.
- Some customer prompts produce extreme skew (e.g., many tokens routed to a single expert) — consider input-based routing regularization (entropy bonus) at admission control.
- In our setup, KV-cache eviction + re-materialization is costly; recommend sticky sessions for long-context customers to avoid repeated cold starts.

Logs / sample commands used (examples):
- nvprof: nvprof --profile-child-processes --print-gpu-trace --csv -o nvprof-llama-4k.csv 
- Nsight: nsys profile --output=nsys-llama-16k ./serve-bench --model llama-13b --seq 16384 --batch 1
- perf logging for MoE: python perf_bench/multi_node_moe.py --experts 8 --topk 2 --seq 8192 --batch 2 --routing gpu --log gs://redwood-perf/logs/2026-02-moe-routing/

References / related tickets:
- PR 412 (GPU routing + pre-alloc dispatch) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- JIRA SRV-3421: Qwen long-context perf regression
- Confluence: Long Context Perf (implementation notes + historical runs)

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers:
- Verify microbenchmarks for correctness after routing-on-GPU change (numerical parity with CPU gating).
- Regression run for embedding/semantics when enabling fused-attn (some models had small accuracy diffs historically).
- Confirm no increased OOMs from pre-alloc KV slabs at peak concurrency.

End of notes.

(Informal — will convert to a cleaner PRD if we lock on mitigations and timelines.)
